(a) **Hardness of Water**: Hardness is the characteristic of water that prevents the lathering of soap and produces insoluble precipitates (scum) due to the presence of dissolved calcium ($\text{Ca}^{2+}$) and magnesium ($\text{Mg}^{2+}$) salts.

(b) **Expressing in $\text{CaCO}_3$ Equivalents**: Calcium carbonate is chosen as the standard reference because:
1. Its molecular mass is exactly 100 g/mol, which makes stoichiometric calculations exceptionally convenient.
2. It is the most insoluble salt that gets precipitated during water treatment.

$$\text{Equivalent of } \text{CaCO}_3 = \frac{\text{Mass of substance} \times \text{Molecular mass of } \text{CaCO}_3 (100)}{\text{Molecular mass of the substance}}$$
proTip: Always mention the molecular weight of $\text{CaCO}_3$ ($100\text{ g/mol}$) when asked about hardness equivalents.
